overview: NetDragon Websoft is a Fuzhou, China-based online games developer and education technology company listed on HKEX since 2008. The Group operates two core segments: Gaming and Application Services (flagship evergreen PC/mobile IP titles such as Eudemons, Conquer and Heroes Evolved, plus AI application services) and Mynd.ai (formerly Gravitas Education, home to the Promethean interactive classroom panel brand), a majority-owned, separately NYSE American-listed education technology subsidiary. Management has pivoted the whole group around a 'Fully Embrace AI' / 'AI Now' strategy covering AIGC game production, AI employees, and AI-native education content.

business_model.summary: Revenue comes from two distinct businesses: (1) high-margin, cash-generative PC/mobile online games and related application services monetized mainly through in-game virtual item sales and subscriptions on long-running ('evergreen') IPs, and (2) Mynd.ai's education hardware (Promethean interactive panels) and increasingly services/SaaS, sold mostly to schools in the US, UK and other developed markets. Group revenue has nearly halved from its FY2022 peak (RMB7.9bn) to RMB4.5bn in FY2025 as both segments contracted - gaming due to deliberate 'flagship IP optimisation' and reduced application-services equity interests, and Mynd.ai due to post-pandemic hardware demand normalization, a prolonged school-budget adjustment cycle, and the FY2024 disposal of the Singapore early-education business.

revenue_streams.name: Gaming and application services
revenue_streams.trend: stabilizing/HoH growth in H1 FY2026 after multi-year decline

business_model.customer_type: B2C (gamers, mostly China and overseas markets like Egypt/MENA for Conquer) for gaming; B2B/B2G (schools, school districts, ministries of education) for Mynd.ai
business_model.geographic_mix: Gaming revenue weighted to China with meaningful overseas contribution (Conquer IP ~70% overseas, strong in Egypt/MENA; Heroes Evolved has PC/esports presence). Mynd.ai sells primarily into the US, UK/Europe. Cash holdings ~79% RMB, ~15% USD, ~6% other currencies (H1 FY2026).

competitive_position.market_position: A mid-tier Chinese online games publisher best known for long-running 'evergreen' IPs (Eudemons Online, Conquer Online, Heroes Evolved) rather than blockbuster new releases; far smaller in scale than Tencent or NetEase. In education hardware, Promethean is a top-tier global brand in K-12 interactive panels (management claims market leadership in several categories) but competes against SMART Technologies, Boxlight, ViewSonic and Chinese low-cost panel makers (Newline, Yushi, Shiyuan) in a commoditizing hardware market.

moat_factors.description: Conquer, Eudemons and Heroes Evolved have run for 15-20+ years with loyal, monetizing communities (MAU still growing YoY), reducing customer acquisition costs versus launching new titles
Decades-old classroom technology brand with an installed base of panels that creates a channel for recurring software/SaaS and services revenue

AI Content Factory and 'AI Employee Matrix' claimed to cut R&D costs materially (segmental R&D down 33% YoY in gaming in FY2025) and could be a genuine cost moat if sustained, though unproven versus peers' own AI adoption
RMB ~1.8-2.0bn net cash and liquid investments provides resilience and funds shareholder returns through a prolonged downturn

weaknesses: No blockbuster new-IP pipeline; growth depends on monetizing aging titles and cost-cutting rather than top-line expansion
Mynd.ai is a structurally lower-margin, cyclical hardware business facing commoditization and Chinese low-cost competition
Small scale versus Tencent/NetEase in gaming and versus SMART/Boxlight in education hardware limits pricing power and R&D budget
Revenue concentration risk in a narrow set of aging IPs for the profitable segment
History of volatile, event-driven profit (crypto holdings, disposals, impairments) complicates underlying earnings assessment

growth_drivers: AI-native game development (Match-3, Roguelike genres) and AI Employee Matrix aiming to cut production costs and speed content release
moyu AI - new AI Workforce Ecosystem/application platform launched August 2026, a potential new monetization vertical beyond gaming and education
Education AIGC ('AI Content Factory') for AI textbooks, courseware and gamified learning content, with new country rollouts (Thailand MHESI, Cameroon MINESEC, Africa pilot via World Bank partnership)
Mynd.ai mix shift toward higher-margin Service/SaaS recurring revenue as hardware demand stabilizes
Strategic partnership with ByteDance's Volcengine for AIGC in China's higher/vocational education market

Hong Kong subsidiary Cherrypicks repositioned as exclusive overseas commercialisation platform for Zhongke WengAI (AI enterprise), developing X-Agent based applications (ScienceOne, Claworks, INSTORE CX)
Continued cost discipline: FY2025 operating expenses down 22.2% YoY, with full benefit expected in FY2026
Gaming + cultural tourism cross-promotion (Fujian provincial partnerships) to re-engage aging IP communities

business.risk: Revenue decline (~43% cumulative from FY2022 to FY2025)
business.description: Both segments have been shrinking; gaming revenue fell due to deliberate IP 'optimisation' and divestment of application-services stakes, Mynd.ai fell due to demand normalization and budget uncertainty
Core profit driver (gaming/application services core segmental profit RMB897m in FY2025) rests on IPs that are 15-20+ years old; no proven new blockbuster to replace them if engagement fades
Core segmental loss of RMB358m in FY2025 (up from RMB297m in FY2024), though narrowing in H1 FY2026; hardware demand cyclicality and school budget uncertainty are industry-wide, not company-specific
Company holds ~12,000 ETH on balance sheet; recognized ~RMB92m impairment in H1 FY2025 tied to crypto price moves, adding non-operating earnings volatility unrelated to the core business

financial.risk: Negative operating and free cash flow
financial.description: Operating cash flow turned negative in H1 FY2024 (-RMB96m FCF) and H1 FY2025 (-RMB63m OCF/-RMB459m FCF); FY2025 OCF recovered to +RMB378m but FCF stayed negative (-RMB146m), and H1 FY2026 OCF/FCF are negative again (-RMB160m/-RMB252m), raising questions about underlying cash generation quality versus reported accounting profit

Gearing ratio (bank borrowings/equity) rose from 0.29 (FY2024) to 0.44 (FY2025), moderating to 0.40 by H1 FY2026; total bank borrowings and other debt of RMB2.5-2.8bn against a shrinking equity base (RMB5.4bn FY2025, down from RMB7.3bn FY2021)

financial.risk: Shareholder return commitment amid cash burn
financial.description: Company has committed to distribute no less than HKD600m over 12 months via dividends/buybacks even as free cash flow has been negative in several recent periods, drawing down net cash (RMB2.0bn end-FY2025 to RMB1.8bn end-H1 FY2026)
Group explicitly has no FX hedging policy; functional currencies span RMB, USD and GBP across PRC, US and UK operations

regulatory.description: Chinese game publishers remain subject to content approval, anti-addiction and playtime restrictions for minors, and periodic regulatory tightening cycles affecting monetization
Mynd.ai's US/UK school customers are exposed to government education budget cycles (e.g., US ESSER funding unwind) which directly drives the 'prolonged demand adjustment cycle' cited by management
Expanding AIGC/education deployments across US, UK, Thailand, Cameroon and other jurisdictions increases exposure to varying data-privacy and AI-governance rules

macro.description: In-game spending by Chinese/overseas gamers is discretionary and sensitive to macro conditions in China and in Conquer's key overseas market (Egypt/MENA)
School hardware refresh cycles are tied to government/public budget health in the US, UK and Europe, and are currently depressed
ETH holdings introduce direct balance-sheet exposure to crypto market swings, as seen in the FY2025 impairment

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese online/PC gaming is a large, mature, but slow-growth market dominated by Tencent and NetEase; evergreen-IP publishers like NetDragon compete on community retention and overseas diversification rather than new hit rates. Global K-12 interactive-display/classroom-technology market is in a post-COVID hardware demand trough, with analysts projecting gradual growth as devices in schools reach replacement age and institutions add AI-enabled software/SaaS layers.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - gaming spend is discretionary consumer behavior; Mynd.ai hardware sales are tied to multi-year government/school capex and procurement cycles, both currently soft
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - Group carries meaningful bank borrowings (~RMB2.0-2.4bn principal) with a mix of fixed/variable rates; higher rates raise finance costs, though most debt appears fixed-rate
key_input_costs: Game server/cloud hosting (and AI compute capacity via Volcengine partnership)
Panel hardware components/display panels for Promethean products

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 interim results: revenue RMB2.1bn (-12.2% YoY) but operating profit +24.1% YoY to RMB144m; gaming segment revenue grew 3.1% HoH signaling stabilization; Mynd.ai core segmental loss narrowed 35.4% YoY; interim dividend of HKD0.50/share declared
Launched moyu AI, a multi-scenario AI Workforce Ecosystem/application platform, at the Global Smart Education Conference
Chairman Liu Dejian announced intention to increase personal shareholding on the open market over the following 12 months, signaling insider confidence

FY2025 annual results: revenue RMB4.5bn (-26.0% YoY), profit attributable to owners RMB151m (-51.4% YoY) impacted by cryptocurrency impairment and one-off staff optimisation costs; operating expenses cut 22.2% YoY; final dividend HKD0.50/share (total HKD1.0/share for FY2025); committed to distribute no less than HKD600m over the following 12 months via dividends/buybacks
H1 2025 results showed profit fell ~92.5% YoY to RMB30m, driven by ~RMB92m cryptocurrency (ETH) impairment and workforce optimisation costs; company held ~12,000 ETH as of 30 June 2025
Hong Kong subsidiary Cherrypicks secured strategic investment from Zhongke WengAI and repositioned as its exclusive overseas expansion/commercialisation platform

Signed partnership with ByteDance's Volcengine for AIGC in China's higher/vocational education sector; cooperation agreements with Thailand's MHESI and Cameroon's MINESEC (with World Bank support) to deploy AI-driven education platforms
MSCI ESG rating upgraded from BBB to A

items.notes: Tied to AI Employee Matrix rollout; management states this should further reduce R&D costs and development cycle times

items.notes: Qualitative target only, aimed at further reducing Mynd.ai segmental operating expenses (down 21.1% YoY in FY2025)

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Liu Dejian framed 2025-2026 as a transition year under the 'AI Now' strategy, emphasizing that cost optimisation benefits would be 'further realised in 2026' and that both gaming and Mynd.ai segments show 'resilient' and 'stabilising' trends despite lower absolute revenue. Management repeatedly stressed confidence in long-term value creation, a conservative/unlevered treasury policy, and continuing the shareholder return programme even through the current revenue downturn.

bull_case: Gaming segment showing genuine stabilization - HoH revenue growth in H1 FY2026, rising MAU on flagship Eudemons IP for five consecutive half-years, and margin expansion from AI-driven cost cuts (core segmental profit margin up 3.9ppts YoY in FY2025)

Mynd.ai losses narrowing sharply (core segmental loss -35.4% YoY in H1 FY2026, adjusted EBITDA loss -53.7% YoY) with SaaS/services revenue growing even as hardware revenue declines, suggesting an eventual path to breakeven

Strong net cash position (~RMB1.8-2.0bn) and conservative, unleveraged treasury policy support a high, explicitly committed dividend/buyback programme (~HKD600m/year) even through the downturn, implying a high trailing dividend yield
Chairman's publicly announced intent to buy more shares personally (March 2026) signals insider confidence near depressed valuations

AI optionality - moyu AI platform, AI Content Factory, and partnerships (Volcengine/ByteDance, Zhongke WengAI, Thailand/Cameroon government deals) could open new monetization avenues beyond the legacy gaming and hardware businesses if execution succeeds
bear_case: Revenue has nearly halved from the FY2022 peak (RMB7.9bn to RMB4.5bn FY2025) with no clear catalyst yet for a sustained reacceleration; current 'stabilization' is from a much lower base

Operating/free cash flow has repeatedly turned negative (H1 FY2024, H1 FY2025, H1 FY2026), raising doubts about the quality and sustainability of reported accounting profit, even as the company maintains a large shareholder-return commitment that could draw down cash reserves further

Both segments lack a clear new growth engine - gaming profit relies on 15-20 year old IPs with no proven blockbuster pipeline, and Mynd.ai operates in a commoditizing, still loss-making hardware category facing low-cost Chinese and established Western competitors

Non-operating earnings volatility - cryptocurrency (ETH) holdings and impairments, disposals, and one-off restructuring costs make reported profit difficult to use as a clean read on the underlying business trend

Rising leverage (gearing ratio up from 0.29 to 0.44 within a year) against a shrinking equity base, combined with ongoing capital returns, constrains financial flexibility if the downturn persists longer than management expects
